title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #15

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is NOT a job of the roots? (1 mark)
   A. Storing food in some plants
   B. Taking in water
   C. Making fruit
   D. Holding the plant in the soil

2. Which of these plant parts is usually colourful? (1 mark)
   A. Soil
   B. Flower
   C. Stem
   D. Root

3. What comes out of a bean seed first when it starts to grow? (1 mark)
   A. A fruit
   B. A root
   C. A new seed
   D. A flower

4. Which of these is a sign of life in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Changing into a stone
   B. Growing taller over time
   C. Making a loud noise
   D. Walking to find water

5. A tadpole grows into a frog. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Animals do not grow
   B. Animals grow and change
   C. Tadpoles are plants
   D. Only fish grow

6. A goat lifts its head when it hears a noise. Which sign of life is this? (1 mark)
   A. Responding to changes
   B. Growing
   C. Reproducing
   D. Breathing out

7. Which group of animals has dry, scaly skin and includes snakes and crocodiles? (1 mark)
   A. Amphibians
   B. Birds
   C. Mammals
   D. Reptiles

8. Which of these is a difference between plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
   B. Animals do not grow
   C. Plants die but animals do not
   D. Plants breathe and animals do not

9. Which of these is a good way to care for a farm animal? (1 mark)
   A. Give it dirty water
   B. Leave it in the rain
   C. Beat it
   D. Give clean water and shelter

10. Which of these is a safe thing to do on a science walk? (1 mark)
   A. Pick up unknown snakes
   B. Tease insects
   C. Throw stones at birds
   D. Wash your hands after touching soil or animals

11. Where does digestion finish and digested food pass into the blood? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Rectum
   C. Stomach
   D. Mouth

12. Why should you limit sweets and sugary drinks? (1 mark)
   A. They make you taller
   B. They cause tooth decay
   C. They make teeth stronger
   D. They help digestion

13. The stomach is described in the lesson as being like (1 mark)
   A. A hard stone
   B. A sharp knife
   C. A long ladder
   D. A stretchy bag

14. What does the stomach do to food? (1 mark)
   A. Cuts it into pieces
   B. Churns it and mixes it with juices
   C. Stores faeces
   D. Takes back water

15. Why is air matter? (1 mark)
   A. It is invisible
   B. It is cold
   C. It is light
   D. It has mass and takes up space

16. How many grams are in 1 kilogram? (1 mark)
   A. 500
   B. 1000
   C. 10
   D. 100

17. What does volume mean? (1 mark)
   A. How heavy it feels
   B. The amount of space an object takes up
   C. The amount of matter in an object
   D. The colour of an object

18. How many millilitres are in 2 litres? (1 mark)
   A. 20
   B. 20 000
   C. 200
   D. 2000

19. Which activity shows that air takes up space? (1 mark)
   A. Singing a song
   B. Blowing up a balloon
   C. Shining a torch
   D. Lighting a candle

20. Steam from a boiling pot is really (1 mark)
   A. A block of ice
   B. A white solid
   C. A red liquid
   D. An invisible gas

21. Why is burning plastic bad? (1 mark)
   A. It is safe for everyone
   B. It makes harmful smoke
   C. It makes rain
   D. It makes good manure

22. Which is an example of reusing? (1 mark)
   A. Burning a plastic bottle
   B. Leaving it on the road
   C. Throwing it in a drain
   D. Using a washed bottle to carry water

23. What should never be done with waste in a place where children are playing? (1 mark)
   A. Put it in a bin
   B. Sort it
   C. Collect it
   D. Burn it

24. Which of these is a result of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. More trees
   B. Less money spent
   C. Less water for others
   D. More rain

25. Why do people spread ash or sand on a slippery path? (1 mark)
   A. To increase friction
   B. To make it hot
   C. To reduce friction
   D. To make it heavy

26. What happens if there is no friction between your shoes and the ground? (1 mark)
   A. You fly
   B. You slip
   C. You stop
   D. You walk faster

27. A force can be small or big. A bigger push makes a ball go (1 mark)
   A. Change colour
   B. Slower
   C. Not move
   D. Faster and further

28. Which of these is translucent? (1 mark)
   A. Tissue paper
   B. Clear glass
   C. Wood
   D. Stone

29. When light hits an opaque object, what forms behind it? (1 mark)
   A. A flame
   B. A rainbow
   C. A shadow
   D. Sound

30. Which of these only reflects light? (1 mark)
   A. The moon
   B. A candle
   C. A torch
   D. A firefly

31. What does a green traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Go
   B. Stop at once
   C. Stop
   D. Sleep

32. Which of these is a safety use of light? (1 mark)
   A. Colouring paint
   B. Street lights
   C. Making shadows
   D. Making sound

33. What is the source of heat that dries fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. A jiko
   B. The sun
   C. Electricity
   D. A torch

34. Which project helps you to handle hot pots safely? (1 mark)
   A. Making a poster
   B. Making kitchen gloves
   C. Making a toy
   D. Making a dustbin

35. How does heat help plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps them warm enough to live
   B. It makes them sleepy
   C. It stops growth
   D. It makes them cold

36. Why do wet clothes dry faster in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. The heat evaporates the water
   B. The sun makes water colder
   C. The sun adds water
   D. The sun makes them heavy

37. Which of these is unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Switching off an iron
   B. Asking an adult to light a fire
   C. Playing with matches
   D. Using gloves

38. In the water cycle, what does heat from the sun do? (1 mark)
   A. Turns water into vapour
   B. Removes all water
   C. Freezes water
   D. Makes water heavy

39. Which of these uses electricity to make heat? (1 mark)
   A. Bicycle
   B. Electric kettle
   C. Wooden chair
   D. Book

40. What should you never do with oil that is on fire? (1 mark)
   A. Call for help
   B. Move away
   C. Cover it with a lid
   D. Pour water on it

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three safety measures during waste management. (3 marks)

42. Describe how you would organise the cleaning of a school compound using safe methods. (5 marks)

43. A pupil says that empty containers have nothing inside. Explain why the pupil is wrong and how you would show it. (5 marks)

44. A tap leaks 4 litres every hour. How much water is lost in 6 hours? (2 marks)

45. Describe the function of each of these parts of a plant: roots, stem, leaves, flowers. (4 marks)

46. Explain the difference between diarrhoea and constipation. (4 marks)

47. State three things that plants give to people. (3 marks)

48. Give two effects of force on objects. (2 marks)

49. Explain how farmers use light to discourage pests and animals. (4 marks)

50. Give three examples of how plants respond to changes around them. (3 marks)

51. A jug holds 500 ml of water. Musa pours in 250 ml and later takes out 100 ml. How much water is in the jug at the end? (4 marks)

52. Explain what gravity is and give two examples of its effects. (3 marks)

53. Describe safety measures to be observed when handling heat at home and at school. (5 marks)

54. Write three safety rules when observing animals in the school compound. (3 marks)

55. Explain how a school can manage waste at the kitchen, classrooms and playground. (4 marks)

56. Give two ways in which animals are different from plants. (2 marks)

57. Name the three main sources of heat. (2 marks)

58. Name two invertebrates that are found near your school. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Making fruit
   Fruits are made from flowers, not by roots.

2. B — Flower
   Flowers are often brightly coloured.

3. B — A root
   The root comes out first and grows down into the soil.

4. B — Growing taller over time
   Plants grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond and die. They do not walk or make noise.

5. B — Animals grow and change
   Young animals grow and may change shape as they become adults.

6. A — Responding to changes
   The goat responds to a change in its surroundings, a sound.

7. D — Reptiles
   Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

8. A — Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
   Most animals move about and eat food, while plants make their own food.

9. D — Give clean water and shelter
   Farm animals need water, food, shelter and care.

10. D — Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
   Handling animals safely and washing hands avoids injury and germs.

11. A — Small intestine
   The small intestine completes digestion and absorbs food into the blood.

12. B — They cause tooth decay
   Sugar feeds germs that damage teeth.

13. D — A stretchy bag
   The stomach is a stretchy bag that churns food.

14. B — Churns it and mixes it with juices
   The stomach churns food into a thick soup with digestive juices.

15. D — It has mass and takes up space
   Air fills balloons and pushes against things, so it takes up space.

16. B — 1000
   1 kg is 1000 g.

17. B — The amount of space an object takes up
   Volume is the space a substance takes up.

18. D — 2000
   2 x 1000 = 2000 ml.

19. B — Blowing up a balloon
   The balloon swells because air takes up space inside.

20. D — An invisible gas
   Steam is water as a gas and is invisible. The cloud we see is tiny water drops.

21. B — It makes harmful smoke
   Burning plastic gives off harmful smoke.

22. D — Using a washed bottle to carry water
   The bottle is used again for a new purpose.

23. D — Burn it
   Burning near children is dangerous.

24. C — Less water for others
   Wasted water is not available to others.

25. A — To increase friction
   Rough material improves grip.

26. B — You slip
   Without friction you cannot grip.

27. D — Faster and further
   A stronger force has a bigger effect.

28. A — Tissue paper
   Tissue paper lets some light through.

29. C — A shadow
   Blocked light makes a shadow.

30. A — The moon
   The moon reflects sunlight.

31. A — Go
   Green means go.

32. B — Street lights
   Street lights help people see at night.

33. B — The sun
   Sun heat dries fish.

34. B — Making kitchen gloves
   Gloves protect hands.

35. A — It keeps them warm enough to live
   Life needs suitable warmth.

36. A — The heat evaporates the water
   Heat makes water turn to vapour.

37. C — Playing with matches
   Matches can start fires.

38. A — Turns water into vapour
   Heat causes evaporation from seas and rivers.

39. B — Electric kettle
   A kettle is heated by electricity.

40. D — Pour water on it
   Water on burning oil spreads the fire.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear gloves and closed shoes, use a rake or shovel, do not touch sharp objects, wash hands afterwards, do not burn waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Form groups with roles. Wear gloves and shoes. Use rakes and shovels. Sort waste into decomposable and non-decomposable bins. Take compost to the pit. Wash hands after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: They are full of air which is matter. Air takes up space. For example the upside-down cup pushed into water stays dry inside or a balloon swells with air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air is matter, 1 mark for an activity, 1 mark for the observation, 1 mark for the conclusion.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: 24 litres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 6 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the plant and take in water. The stem supports the plant and carries water and food. Leaves make food. Flowers make fruits and seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Diarrhoea is passing loose watery faeces many times and causes loss of water. Constipation is passing hard dry faeces with difficulty.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each condition.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Food, shade, wood, medicine, clean air (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Change shape, start motion, stop motion, increase speed, decrease speed, change direction, hold things together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: They use bright or flashing lights at night near fields or animal pens to scare wild animals away. Lamps near sheds help to see thieves or pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bright lights, 1 mark for scaring away animals and 2 marks for examples.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Growing towards light, roots growing down, touch-me-not folding leaves, flowers opening in the day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 500 + 250 = 750, 1 mark for 750 - 100, 1 mark for 650, 1 mark for the unit ml.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity is the force that pulls objects towards the Earth. It makes rain fall and makes a thrown ball come down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each example.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Do not play with matches, keep children from fires, use gloves, turn handles inwards, switch off cookers and irons, keep fuels away from fire, cool burns with water and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each measure up to 5.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not pick up animals you do not know, do not harm animals, wash hands after touching soil or animals, return animals to where they were found.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kitchen: compost pit for food waste and separate bin for plastic. Classroom: bin with lid and paper box. Playground: bins and monitors who pick litter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each place and 1 mark for a clear system.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Animals can move from place to place. Animals feed on ready-made food while plants make their own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct difference.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun, fire and electricity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two correct examples such as ant, earthworm, snail, butterfly, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct invertebrate.
